title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description:
A Tale of Two Cities is an 1859 historical novel by Charles Dickens, set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution. The novel tells the story of the French Doctor Manette, his 18-year-long imprisonment in the Bastille in Paris, and his release to live in London with his daughter Lucie, whom he had never met. The story is set against the conditions that led up to the French Revolution and the Reign of Terror. As one of the most famous works in world literature, it highlights themes of resurrection, social justice, dualities, and the power of sacrifice.

The narrative opens with the iconic phrase, 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' The story follows Lucie Manette as she discovers her father is still alive and helps restore him to sanity. Lucie later marries Charles Darnay, a French aristocrat who has renounced his heritage due to his disgust with the cruelties of his family, the Evrémondes. However, Darnay's noble lineage returns to haunt him when he is drawn back to Paris to save an innocent friend during the height of the Revolution. Captured by the revolutionaries, Darnay faces execution by the guillotine. He is ultimate saved by Sydney Carton, a cynical and disillusioned English barrister who secretly loves Lucie and chooses to trade places with Darnay, sacrificing his own life to secure their happiness.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description:
The Little Prince (Le Petit Prince) is a novella by French aristocrat, writer, and military aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. First published in English and French in the United States in April 1943, it is one of the most translated and best-selling books in history. The story follows a young prince who visits various planets in space, including Earth, addressing themes of loneliness, friendship, love, and loss. Despite its style as a children's book, The Little Prince makes observations about life and human nature that resonate deeply with adult readers.

The narrative begins with an aviator stranded in the Sahara Desert after his plane crashes. While attempting to repair his engine, he meets a extraordinary boy dubbed 'the Little Prince.' The prince shares stories of his small home asteroid, B-612, where he spent his days raking out volcanoes and caring for a beautiful but proud rose. Feeling neglected by the rose, he set off on a journey across the cosmos. Along the way, he visits six other asteroids, each inhabited by an adult who embodies a flawed aspect of society: a king with no subjects, a vain man seeking admiration, a drunkard drinking to forget shame, a businessman counting stars he claims to own, a lamplighter bound by obsolete orders, and a geographer who knows nothing of his own world. Upon arriving on Earth, the prince learns vital life lessons about what truly matters from a wild fox, who teaches him that 'one sees clearly only with the heart; what is essential is invisible to the eye.'

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description:
The Alchemist is an allegorical novel by Brazilian author Paulo Coelho, originally written in Portuguese and published in 1988. An international bestseller, the novel tells the enchanting story of Santiago, an Andalusian shepherd boy who yearns to travel in search of a worldly treasure far more extravagant than any ever found. His quest leads him to riches far different—and far more satisfying—than he ever imagined.

Santiago's journey begins after he experiences a recurring dream about finding a hidden treasure located at the Egyptian pyramids. Seeking an interpretation, he consults a Romani fortune teller and later meets an old king named Melchizedek, who introduces him to the concept of a 'Personal Legend'—a person's true purpose in life. Encouraged to pursue his dream, Santiago sells his sheep and travels to North Africa. Along the way, he faces numerous setbacks, including being robbed in Tangier, which forces him to work for a crystal merchant. Once he earns enough money, he joins a caravan across the Sahara Desert, where he meets an Alchemist who becomes his mentor. The Alchemist teaches Santiago about the 'Soul of the World,' the importance of listening to one's heart, and recognizing omen signals along life's path. Upon reaching the pyramids, Santiago faces a final twist of fate that reveals the true location of his physical treasure lies back where his journey began, teaching him that the journey itself was the ultimate prize.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
description:
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (published in the United States as Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone) is the fantasy novel that launched the globally acclaimed series by British author J. K. Rowling. The novel introduces Harry Potter, a young boy who discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is an orphaned wizard with a mysterious past, setting the stage for one of the most successful franchises in literary and cinematic history.

Raised by his abusive aunt, uncle, and cousin, Harry has lived a miserable existence sleeping in a cupboard under the stairs. Everything changes when he receives a acceptance letter to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, delivered by a half-giant named Rubeus Hagrid. Harry learns that his parents were powerful magical figures murdered by the dark wizard Lord Voldemort, and that Harry miraculously survived Voldemort's killing curse as an infant, leaving him with a lightning-bolt scar and legendary status in the wizarding world. At Hogwarts, Harry makes lifelong friends in Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, and begins his education in magic. However, strange events at the school lead the trio to discover that the Philosopher's Stone—a magical object granting immortality—is hidden within the castle and under threat. Believing a hostile professor is attempting to steal it for the weakened Voldemort, Harry and his friends navigate a series of deadly magical obstacles to protect the stone, confronting the true agent of evil in a dramatic final showdown.

title: And Then There Were None
author: Agatha Christie
description:
And Then There Were None is a mystery novel by English writer Agatha Christie, widely considered her masterpiece and the world's best-selling mystery novel. The plot centers on ten strangers who are lured under various pretexts to an isolated island off the coast of Devon, England, only to be systematically murdered one by one in ways that parallel an ominous nursery rhyme.

Each guest receives an invitation from an unseen host named U.N. Owen (a play on 'Unknown'). Upon arriving at the secluded mansion on Soldier Island, the guests discover their host is absent, and they are left in the care of two newly hired servants. During dinner, a recorded voice plays from a phonograph, accusing each person present of having committed a murder in their past that escaped legal justice. Shortly after the recording finishes, the guests begin dying off in mysterious circumstances that match the verses of the nursery rhyme 'Ten Little Soldiers.' Suspicion mounts rapidly as the survivors realize the killer must be one of them. Trapped by severe storm conditions and with no way off the island, atmosphere turns paranoid and chaotic. As the body count rises and the remaining survivors turn on one another, the novel explores themes of guilt, justice, and human psychology under extreme terror, culminating in a shocking resolution revealed through a postscript message found in a floating bottle.

title: The Hobbit
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description:
The Hobbit, or There and Back Again, is a children's fantasy novel by English author J. R. R. Tolkien. Set in the fictional universe of Middle-earth, the book follows the quest of home-loving hobbit Bilbo Baggins to win a share of the treasure guarded by Smaug the dragon. Bilbo's journey takes him away from his comfortable, rural life into a much more dangerous world.

The story begins in the Shire when the wizard Gandalf arrives at Bilbo's home, accompanied by thirteen dwarves led by Thorin Oakenshield. The dwarves intend to reclaim their ancestral mountain home, the Lonely Mountain, and its vast wealth from the formidable dragon Smaug. Bilbo is recruited as the group's official 'burglar.' Despite initial reluctance and self-doubt, Bilbo embarks on the grand adventure across dangerous lands. Along the journey, the party encounters trolls, goblins, giant spiders, and wood-elves. In a critical encounter deep beneath the Misty Mountains, Bilbo gets separated from the group and finds a mysterious, magical ring that turns its wearer invisible, winning it from a creature named Gollum in a game of riddles. The ring proves invaluable as Bilbo repeatedly saves the dwarves from peril. Ultimately, the quest culminates in the Battle of the Five Armies, where various races unite to defeat invading goblin armies, transforming Bilbo from a timid homebody into a wise and heroic figure.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
description:
To Kill a Mockingbird is a Pulitzer Prize-winning novel by Harper Lee, published in 1960. Instantly successful, it became a classic of modern American literature, exploring themes of racial injustice, destruction of innocence, class, and compassion in the Deep South during the Great Depression.

The story takes place in the fictional town of Maycomb, Alabama, and is narrated by six-year-old Jean Louise 'Scout' Finch. Scout lives with her older brother, Jem, and their widowed father, Atticus Finch, a principled lawyer. Scout and Jem spend their summers playing with their friend Dill and obsessing over their reclusive, mysterious neighbor, Arthur 'Boo' Radley, whom town rumors paint as a monster. The central plot of the novel unfolds when Atticus is appointed to defend Tom Robinson, a Black man falsely accused of raping a young white woman, Mayella Ewell. Despite overwhelming evidence proving Tom's innocence and demonstrating that Mayella's abusive father pushed her to lie, the all-white jury convicts Tom due to pervasive racial prejudice. This trial shatters Jem and Scout's moral world, forcing them to confront the grim realities of bigotry and hypocrisy. Meanwhile, the children discover that Boo Radley is actually a gentle protector who ultimately saves them from a vengeful physical attack by Mayella's father, reinforcing Atticus's lesson that it is a sin to harm something innocent like a mockingbird.

author: George Orwell
description:
Nineteen Eighty-Four is a dystopian novel by English author George Orwell, published in 1949. The novel examines the dangers of totalitarianism, mass surveillance, and repressive regimentation of persons and behaviors within society, introducing famous concepts like 'Big Brother,' 'Thought Police,' and 'Doublethink.'

The story is set in a terrifying future where Great Britain, now part of a superstate called Oceania, is ruled by 'The Party' led by the enigmatic figurehead Big Brother. The Party exercises total control over its citizens through continuous surveillance via two-way telescreens, relentless propaganda, and the manipulation of history through the Ministry of Truth. The protagonist, Winston Smith, works at the Ministry of Truth altering historical records to align with official Party narratives. Secretly hating the totalitarian regime, Winston begins keeping a illegal diary expressing his rebellious thoughts. He enters into a forbidden love affair with Julia, a fellow worker, and together they seek out an underground resistance organization known as the Brotherhood. However, their attempts at rebellion fail when they are betrayed by O'Brien, a high-ranking Party member posing as a fellow rebel. Winston is arrested and subjected to systematic torture and psychological re-education in Room 101, designed to break his spirit until he genuinely loves Big Brother.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
description:
The Great Gatsby is a 1925 novel by American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald, set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, near New York City. The novel depicts first-person narrator Nick Carraway's interactions with mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and Gatsby's obsession to reunite with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan.

Nick Carraway, a young Yale graduate from the Midwest, rents a small house in West Egg next door to the colossal mansion of Jay Gatsby, who hosts lavish, extravagant parties every weekend open to anyone. Unlike his guests, Gatsby remains elusive and quiet. Nick soon learns that Gatsby's excessive wealth and glamorous lifestyle were built solely to attract Daisy Buchanan, Nick's cousin, who lives across the bay in East Egg with her wealthy, arrogant husband, Tom. Five years prior, Gatsby and Daisy had a passionate romance before Gatsby left to fight in World War I; Daisy subsequently married Tom. With Nick's help, Gatsby and Daisy reunite and reignite their secret affair. Tensions escalate when Tom uncovers their relationship, leading to a fiery confrontation in New York. On the drive back, Daisy accidentally strikes and kills Tom's mistress, Myrtle Wilson, while driving Gatsby's car. Gatsby takes responsibility for the accident to protect Daisy, leading Myrtle's grieving husband to murder Gatsby, leaving Nick disillusioned with the tragic hollow reality of the American Dream.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description:
Pride and Prejudice is an 1813 romantic novel of manners written by Jane Austen. The novel follows the character development of Elizabeth Bennet, the dynamic protagonist who learns about the repercussions of hasty judgments and comes to appreciate the difference between superficial goodness and actual goodness.

The story revolves around the Bennet family, including five unmarried daughters whose mother is desperate to find them wealthy husbands to secure their financial futures. When the rich, eligible bachelor Charles Bingley rents a nearby estate in Hertfordshire, he quickly falls in love with Elizabeth's gentle older sister, Jane. However, Bingley's haughty and even wealthier friend, Fitzwilliam Darcy, initial causes offense at a local ball by refusing to dance with Elizabeth and insulting her appearance. Elizabeth develops a strong dislike for Darcy, which is further reinforced by the charming militia officer George Wickham, who paints Darcy as a cruel villain. Over time, Elizabeth rejects a marriage proposal from Darcy due to his arrogant attitude and involvement in separating Bingley and Jane. In response, Darcy writes a letter clarifying the truth behind Wickham's deceitful character and his own actions. Elizabeth is forced to re-evaluate her prideful assumptions, ultimately realizing Darcy's true nobility and falling deeply in love with him.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J. D. Salinger
description:
The Catcher in the Rye is a novel by J. D. Salinger, published in 1951. Originally intended for adults, it became famous for its iconic portrayal of teenage angst, alienation, identity, and critique of superficiality in adult society.

The novel is narrated by Holden Caulfield, a 16-year-old boy who has just been expelled from his prep school, Pencey Prep, due to failing most of his classes. Unwilling to return home to his parents in New York City before his official break begins, Holden decides to wander New York City alone for several days. Throughout his journey, Holden struggles with profound feelings of isolation, grief over the tragic death of his younger brother Allie, and disgust toward what he views as the 'phoniness' of the adult world. He experiences a series of awkward and depressing encounters with various acquaintances, hotel staff, and strangers. The only person Holden connects with genuinely is his younger sister, Phoebe. When Phoebe asks what he wants to do with his life, Holden describes an idealized fantasy based on a misheard poem: standing in a field of rye near a cliff and catching children before they fall off—symbolizing his desire to preserve childhood innocence from the corruption of growing up.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
description:
The Da Vinci Code is a 2003 mystery-thriller novel by Dan Brown that follows Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon and cryptologist Sophie Neveu as they investigate a murder in the Louvre Museum in Paris.

The plot begins when Jacques Saunière, the Louvre's grand curator, is murdered inside the museum. Before dying, Saunière arranges his own body in a dramatic pose mimicking the Vitruvian Man and leaves behind a series of cryptic riddles, numerical codes, and symbols written in his own blood. Robert Langdon is brought in as a consultant by French police captain Bezu Fache, who secretly suspects Langdon of the crime. Sophie Neveu, Saunière's estranged granddaughter, arrives and warns Langdon that he is being framed, helping him escape. Together, Langdon and Sophie follow the clues left by Saunière, uncovering a trail that leads to the works of Leonardo da Vinci. They discover that Saunière was the head of the Priory of Sion, a secret society protecting an ancient secret: that Jesus Christ was married to Mary Magdalene and bore descendants, and that the Holy Grail is actually Mary's tomb and bloodline. Pursued by both the police and a fanatic opus dei monk named Silas who wishes to destroy the secret, the duo races across France and the UK to unlock the Holy Grail's mystery.

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
author: Gabriel García Márquez
description:
One Hundred Years of Solitude (Cien años de soledad) is a landmark 1967 novel by Colombian author Gabriel García Márquez. Considered a masterpiece of magical realism and world literature, the book tells the multi-generational story of the Buendía family, whose patriarch, José Arcadio Buendía, founded the fictional South American town of Macondo.

The narrative spans a century in Macondo, tracing the rise and fall of both the town and the seven generations of the Buendía family. José Arcadio Buendía and his wife, Úrsula Iguarán, establish Macondo as an isolated, idyllic village in the swamp. Over decades, the town becomes connected to the outside world, undergoing civil wars, political corruption, technological changes, and economic exploitation by a foreign banana company. Throughout the novel, realistic historical events are seamlessly blended with surreal, magical elements—such as a girl floating into the sky while folding laundry, yellow butterflies following a lover, and a rain of yellow flowers. The recurring themes of tragic solitude, cyclical time, and fatalistic destiny plague every member of the family, as repeated names and personality traits pass down through generations. Ultimately, after years of civil decline, a catastrophic hurricane wipes Macondo off the earth just as the last Buendía decipher ancient manuscripts predicting their complete destruction.

title: The Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description:
Crime and Punishment is an 1866 psychological novel by Russian author Fyodor Dostoevsky. Set in Saint Petersburg, it focuses on the mental anguish and moral dilemmas of an impoverished former student who formulates a theory regarding extraordinary human beings.

The protagonist, Rodion Raskolnikov, lives in extreme poverty in Saint Petersburg. He formulates a dangerous philosophical theory that society is divided into ordinary people and extraordinary individuals who have the right to break moral laws and commit crimes if it serves a higher purpose. To test his theory and solve his financial troubles, Raskolnikov murders a cruel, greedy elderly pawnbroker with an axe, as well as her innocent sister who witnesses the crime. Immediately after the murders, Raskolnikov is overwhelmed by intense horror, paranoia, and psychological torment rather than feeling like a heroic figure. As physical illness and guilt consume him, he becomes entangled in a high-stakes psychological game with Porfiry Petrovich, the brilliant police investigator suspecting him. Raskolnikov eventually forms a bond with Sonya Marmeladova, a pious young woman forced into prostitution to support her family. Moved by Sonya's selfless compassion and faith, Raskolnikov confesses his crime, accepts exile to Siberia, and embarks on a long path toward spiritual redemption.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description:
Jane Eyre is a novel by English writer Charlotte Brontë, published under the pen name 'Currer Bell' in 1847. Famous for its emotional intensity and strong first-person voice, the novel follows the growth of an orphaned girl into adulthood and her love for the enigmatic Edward Rochester.

The story traces Jane's life through five distinct stages: her childhood at Gateshead Hall with her cruel aunt and cousins; her harsh education at Lowood School; her time as a governess at Thornfield Hall; her stay with her relatives the Rivers at Moor House; and her eventual reunion with Rochester. At Thornfield Hall, Jane is hired to tutor Adèle, the ward of the brooding, sarcastic master of the house, Edward Rochester. Despite their differences in social status, Jane and Rochester develop a profound intellectual and emotional connection, leading to a proposal of marriage. However, on their wedding day, Jane discovers a devastating secret: Rochester is already married to Bertha Mason, a woman who went insane and is locked away in the attic of Thornfield Hall. Refusing to compromise her moral principles by becoming Rochester's mistress, Jane flees into the night. After building an independent life, Jane eventually returns to Thornfield to find it burned down and Rochester blinded; with her independence secured, she marries him as his equal.

title: The Lord of the Rings
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
description:
The Lord of the Rings is an epic high-fantasy novel written by English author J. R. R. Tolkien. Set in Middle-earth, the story began as a sequel to Tolkien's 1937 fantasy novel The Hobbit, but eventually developed into a much larger work written in stages between 1937 and 1949.

The epic centers on the One Ring, created by the Dark Lord Sauron to rule over all the other Rings of Power and conquer Middle-earth. The ring has fallen into the hands of a young hobbit named Frodo Baggins in the quiet Shire. Realizing Sauron is seeking the Ring to regain his full power, the wizard Gandalf directs Frodo to leave his home. A Fellowship of nine representatives—including Hobbits (Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin), Men (Aragorn and Boromir), an Elf (Legolas), a Dwarf (Gimli), and Gandalf—is formed to protect Frodo on a quest to destroy the Ring in the fires of Mount Doom, the only place it was forged.

As the Fellowship journeys across Middle-earth, they face overwhelming corruption, battles against armies of Orcs, and internal conflict. The Fellowship breaks, leaving Frodo and his loyal servant Samwise Gamgee to trek alone into the dark land of Mordor, guided by the treacherous Gollum. Meanwhile, Aragorn embraces his true destiny as King of Gondor, leading armies of free peoples against Sauron's forces to distract the Dark Lord while Frodo completes his perilous mission.

title: Fahrenheit 451
author: Ray Bradbury
description:
Fahrenheit 451 is a 1953 dystopian novel by American writer Ray Bradbury. Regarded as one of his best works, the novel presents a future American society where books are outlawed and 'firemen' burn any that are found.

The protagonist, Guy Montag, is a fireman in a futuristic city where television screens dominate living rooms and hedonistic entertainment keeps the populace passive and unthinking. In this society, instead of putting out fires, firemen start them to burn illegal books, which are viewed as sources of conflict and unhappiness. Montag takes pride in his work until he meets a free-spirited teenage neighbor, Clarisse McClellan, whose curious worldview and questioning nature spark a transformation within him. Shortly after, Montag witnesses an elderly woman choose to be burned alive with her home rather than surrender her private library. Horrified by the event, Montag secretly steals a book and begins reading, questioning his life, his distant wife Mildred, and his society. Montag seeks out Faber, a retired English professor, to understand the value of literature. When his wife turns him in, Montag is forced by his captain, Beatty, to burn his own house. Montag kills Beatty in self-defense and escapes the city, joining a covert group of exiles who memorize entire books to preserve human knowledge for future generations.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
description:
The Count of Monte Cristo is an adventure novel by French author Alexandre Dumas, completed in 1844. Set in France, Italy, and islands in the Mediterranean during the historical events of 1815–1838, it is a timeless tale of betrayal, revenge, justice, and redemption.

The story centers on Edmond Dantès, a young, promising French merchant sailor about to become captain of his ship and marry his beloved Mercédès. On his wedding day, he is falsely accused of treason by jealous rivals—Fernand Mondego, Danglars, and Gérard de Villefort—and imprisoned without trial in the grim island fortress of Château d'If. During fourteen years of agonizing imprisonment, Dantès meets an elderly Italian priest, Abbé Faria, who becomes his tutor and reveals the location of a vast treasure hidden on the uninhabited island of Monte Cristo. Following Faria's death, Dantès executes a miraculous escape, retrieves the treasure, and reinventing himself as the wealthy and enigmatic Count of Monte Cristo. Armed with immense wealth and wisdom, Dantès travels to Paris to exact meticulous, devastating revenge on the corrupt men who framed him, destroying their fortunes, reputations, and families before discovering that true justice belongs to God and finding personal peace.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
description:
Dune is a 1965 science fiction novel by American author Frank Herbert, winner of the inaugural Nebula Award and Hugo Award. Set in the distant future amidst a feudal interstellar empire, the novel explores complex political, religious, ecological, and technological themes.

The story takes place on the desert planet Arrakis (also known as Dune), the universe's only source of Melange—also called 'the spice'—a invaluable substance that extends human life, grants prescient mental abilities, and enables space navigation. Duke Leto Atreides is assigned stewardship of Arrakis by the Emperor, replacing their bitter blood rivals, the ruthless House Harkonnen. However, the move is a trap concocted by the Emperor and Baron Harkonnen to eradicate House Atreides. Following a brutal ambush, Duke Leto is killed, but his concubine Lady Jessica and his young son Paul Atreides escape into the harsh, unforgiving desert. Paul and Jessica are taken in by the Fremen, the resilient native inhabitants of Arrakis. Among the Fremen, Paul fulfills ancient prophecies of a savior known as the Kwisatz Haderach. Embracing the name Muad'Dib, Paul leads a Fremen rebellion against Harkonnen rule, gaining control over the spice trade and reshaping the political destiny of the galaxy.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description:
Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus is an 1818 novel written by English author Mary Shelley. It tells the story of Victor Frankenstein, a young scientist who creates a sapient creature in an unorthodox scientific experiment, and explores the terrifying consequences of playing God.

The story is framed through letters written by Captain Robert Walton, an Arctic explorer who rescues a dying Victor Frankenstein from the ice. Victor recounts his tragic life story: obsessed with discovering the secret of life, he spends years studying alchemy and modern science at university. Assembling body parts collected from slaughterhouses and graveyards, Victor successfully animates a towering creature. However, horrified by the hideous appearance of his creation, Victor abandons the newborn monster in terror. Left alone, the creature wanders the countryside, secretly observing a peasant family to learn human language, emotions, and morality. Despite his gentle nature and desire for companionship, the creature is violently rejected by everyone he meets due to his terrifying appearance. Consumed by loneliness and anger at his creator, the creature vows revenge on Victor. He demands that Victor build him a female companion; when Victor refuses, the creature murders Victor's brother, best friend, and bride Elizabeth, leading to a tragic, deadly pursuit across the frozen North.
